annotation.authors_or_issuer: Madiega, T.; Van De Pol, A.L. (European Parliamentary Research Service)
key_provisions_or_claims: AI Act proposal Arts. 53-54 introduce voluntary national AI regulatory sandboxes supervised by competent authorities, coordinated via a European AI board.
Sandbox participants remain liable for harm to third parties; critics say this discourages participation.
Further processing of personal data in sandboxes for public-interest AI raises GDPR purpose-limitation concerns.
Risks include regulatory arbitrage, forum-shopping and fragmentation of the single market.
Priority sandbox access for SMEs and start-ups (Art. 55); Parliament's IMCO/LIBE draft report asks for more transparency.
annotation.summary_en: European Parliamentary Research Service briefing on AI regulatory sandboxes in the Commission's 2021 AI Act proposal (Arts. 53-55). It outlines benefits and risks of sandboxes, and stakeholder concerns on liability, fragmentation and GDPR interplay, plus Parliament's positions.
